description: What one crop needs at one stage of its year. KEYED ON THE STAGE AND NOT ON THE MONTH, because bloom moves a fortnight between a warm spring and a cold one, and a schedule pinned to 'April' waters the wrong week in both of them. An irrigation plan asks which stage the block is in and reads a rate; mapping stage to date is the season's job, not the species'. Two rows may not name the same stage — the parent refuses it, because two answers to 'how much water at bloom' is the same as none.

fields.description: The phenological stage this row is about. A FIXED LIST ON PURPOSE, unlike almost everything else in this app that is left free text: these seven are the stages an irrigation decision actually branches on, and a free-text stage would let one crop say 'bloom' and another 'flowering' and the lookup match neither. Post-Harvest is in the list because it is the one everybody forgets and the one that sets next year's fruit bud.
fields.label: Growth Stage
fields.options:
Dormant
Bud Break
Bloom
Fruit Set
Fruit Development
Harvest
Post-Harvest

fields.description: The crop coefficient: what this crop at this stage uses as a fraction of reference evapotranspiration. Typically 0.2 dormant to about 1.2 in full canopy, and values above 1.5 are refused as a transcription error rather than stored. THIS IS THE COLUMN THAT TRAVELS — a Kc is multiplied by whatever ET the weather gives, so it stays right in a hot year and a cool one, which `water_inches_per_week` beside it does not.
fields.label: Crop Coefficient (Kc)

fields.description: A flat weekly depth in inches for this stage, for the operation that plans off a rule of thumb rather than off ET. THE CRUDER OF THE TWO COLUMNS AND DELIBERATELY OFFERED ANYWAY: most farms schedule this way, and a record that only accepted a Kc would be a record most farms could not fill in. Where both are present the Kc is the better number and a reader should prefer it.
fields.label: Water (in/week)

fields.description: What the two numbers do not say — 'hold back to firm the fruit', 'stop two weeks before pick to avoid cracking'. Deficit irrigation is a deliberate practice on cherries and it looks like an under-watered block to anyone reading rates alone.
fields.label: Notes

name: Crop Water Requirement
